headline: GOOG surged nearly 5% last night ahead of earnings — your biggest single-day mover — while the ASX dipped slightly today and lithium headwinds keep PLS under pressure.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG jumped nearly 5% last night on the NASDAQ, likely driven by pre-earnings excitement — the market is pricing in a strong result ahead of Alphabet's upcoming quarterly report. This was your biggest mover of the session, pushing your GOOG position firmly into profit territory (+14% overall).

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO climbed 3.6% last night. There's a Fortune profile doing the rounds about Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick betting $1 billion on GTA VI being the decade's biggest game launch — that kind of hype keeps sentiment around the stock elevated. Your position is now up ~7.8% overall.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed up 2.5% today, riding the coattails of a strong AI/tech session on Wall Street last night (NASDAQ +2%). Still slightly underwater overall (-4%), but trending in the right direction as AI names stayed in favour.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up 1.3% today, reflecting last night's strong S&P 500 (+1.2%) and NASDAQ (+2%) performance feeding through into the ASX-listed ETF. Your position is up 3.8% overall.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL edged up 1.1% today despite oil prices dipping slightly (WTI crude fell 0.7% to US$70.26). Energy stocks got a mild lift from the broader market rally. Worth noting a new forecast sees Brent crude in a $70–$75 range through 2027 on a forecast 4.8 million barrel-per-day surplus — not great for energy stocks longer-term.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped 1.2% today to $5.02. Lithium prices fell 30% recently as sodium-ion batteries gain traction as a cheaper alternative, and China supply continues to flood the market. Your PLS position is now down 25.5% overall — the structural headwinds here are real and ongoing.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT dipped 1.2% last night to $368.57, giving back some of its recent gains. The market may be rotating into Google ahead of earnings season, with GOOG stealing the AI spotlight for now. Microsoft has its own earnings date set for July — that'll be the next big catalyst to watch. Your MSFT position remains down 16.8% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.9% today, a quiet but positive session for emerging markets. Your position is barely in the black (+0.6% overall) — this one moves slowly and is largely driven by China and broader EM sentiment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG crept up 0.3% today — a steady-as-she-goes day for this diversified ETF. With around 90% in growth assets spread globally, it tends to track the broader market mood. Your position is up 2.6% overall.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings coming — big moment for your position
watch_today.detail: Alphabet is in the earnings spotlight this week, with two news items flagging Monday as a key date for the stock. GOOG jumped ~5% last night in what looks like pre-earnings enthusiasm. If results disappoint, that move could reverse fast. Your position is up 14% overall — worth deciding if you'd take profit or hold through the print.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings in July — watch for cloud update
watch_today.detail: Microsoft has flagged its July earnings date and the market is watching closely for an update on Azure cloud growth and AI revenue. MSFT dipped 1.2% last night while Google surged, suggesting some rotation is happening between the two. Your MSFT position is down 16.8% overall — no reason to sell before earnings, but keep expectations in check.

watch_today.title: PLS — structural headwinds are getting harder to ignore
watch_today.detail: Lithium spot prices have dropped 30% recently, with sodium-ion batteries emerging as a cheaper alternative and Chinese supply still flooding the market. UBS does favour a handful of lithium stocks post-pullback, but Pilbara is down 25.5% in your portfolio. No imminent catalyst to recover that loss — this one needs patience or a re-evaluation of your thesis.

watch_today.title: TTWO riding GTA VI hype — solid momentum
watch_today.detail: A Fortune deep-dive on Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick (who reportedly doesn't even play video games) highlights the $1 billion bet on GTA VI being the decade's biggest game launch. The stock is up 3.6% from last night and +7.8% in your portfolio. No reason to sell into strength — let the GTA VI story play out.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — good news for Aussie borrowers and growth stocks
watch_today.detail: The RBA kept interest rates on hold this week and signalled it's comfortable waiting before making any moves. One briefing suggests near-zero rates could eventually return, though the RBA also warned unions that inflation expectations are too high. For you as an investor, steady rates are a tailwind for growth-oriented ETFs like VDHG and GXAI.

watch_today.title: Oil price outlook soft — watch FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: A new forecast projects Brent crude in the $70–$75 range through 2027, based on a 4.8 million barrel-per-day global surplus. WTI oil is already sitting at $70.26. FUEL.AX ticked up today, but the medium-term outlook for energy companies is muted if oil stays range-bound. No need to act now, but worth watching.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street was a strong session — the NASDAQ jumped 2.1% and the S&P 500 gained 1.2%, largely on the back of big tech momentum with Google leading the charge. Closer to home, the ASX 200 slipped 0.5% today to 8,778 points — a mild pullback that didn't dampen the broader mood. Oil edged down slightly to $70.26 a barrel, gold ticked up to $4,044, and the Aussie dollar softened a touch to 68.79 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Mild pullback today — gave back some recent gains but nothing alarming.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Strong session last night, broad-based gains across US markets.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech roared last night — Google's pre-earnings run was a big driver.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Nudged lower — soft demand outlook and OPEC supply keeping a lid on prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Crept higher — still near record levels as investors stay cautious.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar slipped slightly — not a big move, but worth watching for US holdings.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated Australian news today, holding rates steady and signalling patience. Meanwhile the federal government is cracking down harder on tech giants over the under-16 social media ban, and a rushed industrial relations bill is drawing fire from business groups.

stories.title: RBA holds rates, signals it's in no rush to move
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA left interest rates on hold this week, and CommBank's analysis suggests the central bank is happy to sit and wait rather than rush into cuts. One AFR briefing floated the idea that near-zero rates could return sooner than markets expect, though the RBA separately warned that union-driven inflation expectations are still too high for comfort. For everyday Aussies, this means mortgage repayments stay where they are for now — and for investors, stable rates are generally good news for growth assets like shares and ETFs.

stories.title: Government doubles fines to $99M as tech giants face under-16 social media crackdown
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has doubled the maximum penalty for tech companies breaching the under-16 social media ban to $99 million. Communications Minister Michelle Rowland says big tech companies are actively trying to make the laws fail, and the government has signalled this won't be its last move — more tweaks to online safety rules are coming. For investors with exposure to Alphabet (Google/YouTube) or Meta, this is a regulatory pressure point, though Australia alone won't move the needle on those stocks.

stories.title: Rushed industrial relations bill draws 'Victorian disease' warning from business
stories.why_it_matters: Business groups are sounding the alarm over an industrial relations bill being rushed through federal parliament, warning it brings 'Victorian disease' — a reference to Victoria's more union-friendly labour laws — to the national stage. Critics say the speed of the legislation is preventing proper consultation. If the bill passes, it could increase labour costs for businesses, which is a mild headwind for Australian equities more broadly.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is regulatory pressure building from multiple directions — a US poll shows voters across both parties want tighter AI rules, Europe just greenlit simplified AI regulations, and America's patchwork approach is drawing criticism. Plus, a clutch of 'all-in-one AI subscription' deals are circulating if you're looking to consolidate your AI tools.

stories.title: US voters across party lines want AI regulated — poll
stories.why_it_matters: A new NBC News/tech.co poll finds a majority of Americans — regardless of whether they vote Democrat or Republican — want stronger government oversight of AI. This is notable because it removes the usual partisan excuse for inaction. For companies like Google and Microsoft that are betting big on AI, tighter regulation could mean higher compliance costs and slower deployment of new products. It's not an immediate threat, but it's a growing headwind for the sector.

stories.title: Europe's AI Council gives final green light to streamlined rules
stories.why_it_matters: The EU Council has given final approval to a simplified version of its AI Act, streamlining the rules rather than adding complexity. The move is designed to make it easier for companies to comply without drowning in red tape. This is actually mildly positive news for AI-heavy companies operating in Europe — it removes some uncertainty that had been hanging over the sector. Your GXAI.AX ETF has exposure to global AI companies that operate in Europe.

stories.title: America's AI policy called 'truly chaotic' as regulation debate drags on
stories.why_it_matters: A commentary piece describes the US approach to AI regulation as 'truly chaotic' — with different states passing different rules, federal inaction, and the Trump administration pulling in multiple directions. For US-listed AI companies like Google and Microsoft, this patchwork creates unpredictability. The lack of a clear national framework means companies are essentially navigating 50 different rule sets, which adds compliance cost and legal risk down the track.

sport.summary: Wimbledon is underway with a few big storylines — Jannik Sinner survived a first-round scare, the Aussies had mixed Day 1 results, and Serena Williams is back in the conversation. In the NRL, Round 18 team lists are out with a notable shake-up in the Tigers squad. AFL trade whispers are heating up with the mid-season window approaching.

stories.title: Sinner nearly made unwanted Wimbledon history in first-round scare
stories.why_it_matters: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner came dangerously close to a first-round upset at Wimbledon 2026, which would have been a historic embarrassment for a top seed. He ultimately survived, but it was far from convincing. The top half of the draw suddenly looks a little more open if Sinner isn't firing on all cylinders on grass.

stories.title: Aussies find relief on Wimbledon Day 1 despite form concerns
stories.why_it_matters: Australian players had a mixed but ultimately positive Day 1 at Wimbledon 2026, with Fox Sports reporting some form concerns heading into the tournament were overcome. No full scorelines in the article text, but the mood in the Aussie camp is described as 'relief' rather than celebration — suggesting it wasn't smooth sailing.

stories.title: NRL Round 18 team news: Star Tiger scratched, Twal and Willison make shock returns
stories.why_it_matters: With Round 18 kicking off Friday night (Panthers vs Rabbitohs at CommBank Stadium), the Gold Coast Bulletin reports a notable shake-up in the Wests Tigers lineup — a star player has been scratched while Josh Twal and Willison make surprise returns. The Broncos host the Sharks at Suncorp on Saturday night, which is the local game to watch on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: AFL trade whispers: Roos throw 'kitchen sink' at star, Dees dangle top picks
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade whispers are heating up mid-season — North Melbourne are reportedly going all-in to sign a star player, while Melbourne are dangling top draft picks to attract talent. Fox Sports names this the 'September-shaping fortnight' where the most important games of the season will be played. The AFL is also under scrutiny after questions about a concussion incident where the league allegedly failed to intervene at the right time.
